messages.author: f49bc37736374e63
messages.subject: how to define forced ODE
parts:
Hello,

I am just beginning to use Stan, in particular I need it for ODE parameter estimation. Let's say I have an equation:

dy/dt = alpha * (y - forcing)

where y is data at nt time-points and forcing is provided over time at those same time-points. As I understand x_r would pass forcing to the function to be integrated, but it is not really clear how to do that in the Stan documentation. Is there an example you can share on how to do this?

Thanks
Jorge

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: how to define forced ODE
parts:
Hi!

This possibly not the simplest example, but this Stan model

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/feature/issue-72-stan-pkpdlib/misc/pkpd/oral_1cmt_mm.stan

calculates a saturable elimination from a compartement into which first-order dosing is applied. So the forcing is the first-order dosing (resulting in an exponential input term ct in the main cmt). For the specific case above, the parameters of the forcing functions are also parameters of the model, which is why the exponential rate is taken from the theta array instead of the x_r array. In your case the parameters of the forcing function would come from the x_r array (which you really should do if it applies in order to get the numerical burden down).

I hope this helps.

Best,
Sebastian
